A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TCPR research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite the new format and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic simulations and Yummly-10k and anime-ranking evaluations in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices D–E, including coverage, interval-length, and oracle comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Corollary B.1 add postprocessing that converts full-sample rank intervals into intervals for ranks among test items by subtracting bounds on calibration-item counts. Top-K selection generalizes the existing rank-1 example. The underlying scores, envelopes, and calibration procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the Gaussian/logistic synthetic data, the Beta-distribution adaptivity example, Yummly-10k, and anime recommendation. The Beta example moves from v2 Appendix C.2 to v3 Section 5.1. The new theoretical targets introduce no new evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Oracle remains the reference comparison, with the same RA/VA scores, linear/quantile envelopes, and RankNet, LambdaMART, RankSVM, and BRE experiments. The newly cited Bradley–Terry–Luce inference methods are not added to the empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 corrects the stated test size for Figure 2 from m = 2500 to m = 500. The v2 caption and plot already specify m = 500, so this corrects the reported setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. Splits, size grids, metrics, and model settings otherwise match.

E4.justification: The calibration/test-size sensitivity plots, RA-versus-VA adaptivity analysis, oracle comparisons, and dish-selection case study are retained. Moving the Beta example into the main text adds no new analysis or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both report 1000 generated datasets per synthetic size pair and 10 Yummly splits, with the same boxplot/mean displays and Table 1 uncertainty reporting. No new run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 values and matched plotted results are unchanged. For example, RankNet's RA FCP remains 0.069 ± 0.005 and relative length remains 0.306 ± 0.003. The dish example still reports 14 TCPR candidates versus 10 oracle candidates.

T1.justification: v3 adds derived Corollaries B.1–B.2 and proofs for test-only rank intervals and expected top-K recovery, while retaining the central envelope and coverage theory. Theorem 3.5 also introduces an assumption-reference inconsistency: it cites Y-exchangeability, whereas v2 Theorem 4 and the retained proof require joint exchangeability of features and ranks.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph, and conclusion retain the same main claims: distribution-free rank prediction using proxy-score bounds, marginal coverage, FCP control, and empirical efficiency.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix B add applicability discussion for ranks within the test set and top-K selection, including an expected-recovery interpretation. Existing explanations of conservatism and adaptivity, and limitations concerning partial ranking and envelope choice, are retained.

D1.justification: The code availability statement, PyTorch/LightGBM implementations, RankNet architecture, training sizes, and LambdaMART configuration details are retained. Relocation and explanatory clarifications do not establish new implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds discussion of uncertainty quantification under Bradley–Terry–Luce models, including Liu et al. (2023), Gao et al. (2023), and Fan et al. (2025), plus foundational model citations. Appendix A.5 adds the original DKW citation. Existing CP positioning remains.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with localized wording and cross-reference corrections. v3 adds Section 3.3 and Appendix B, relocates the adaptivity discussion into Section 5.1, and updates author information and reference formatting.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS format substantially changes typography, text density, the title/author block, and figure/table placement. Figure 1 and Algorithm 1 now sit beside text; the adaptivity plot moves into the main text as Figure 3; appendix displays are resized and rearranged. The plotted content itself is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a test-only rank construction and improves research positioning, but its new Corollary B.2 is false as written: it counts only test items while defining top K by ranks among all n+m items. With n = m = K = 100 and alpha = 0.1, only 50 true top-K test items exist on average, yet Eq. (21) requires at least 90 recovered. This introduces a limited theoretical overclaim while the core method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
